text: The itertools module is a toolbox of iteration superpowers, all lazy and memory-efficient.
count gives you an endless counter — here starting at one and stepping by two, forever.
Since it never ends, you pull values with next, taking exactly as many as you want.
[chuckle] chain glues several sequences together into one smooth stream, without copying them.
So three separate lists iterate as if they were a single continuous list.
[sniff] combinations generates every possible pairing from a sequence, order not mattering.
From A, B, C it produces A-B, A-C, and B-C — incredibly handy for comparisons and puzzles.
[sigh] cycle repeats a sequence endlessly, so we use islice to safely grab just the first five.
[groan] itertools turns tricky iteration problems into a single, readable line — it's worth exploring the whole module.
Up next, sorting by a key. Follow so you don't miss it.
